patch.value: The docstring gate is fail-open for exported bindings it cannot decompose

Found by Greptile on PR 33 and confirmed by reading parseExportedVar. The gate judges an exported const, let or var by its first leading identifier only, which is fail-open twice in a gate whose entire value is being fail-closed. An export with several declarators leaves every binding after the first unjudged. Worse, an export whose binding is a destructuring pattern starts on a brace rather than an identifier, so nothing is judged at all and an undocumented export walks straight through. The first case is mostly cosmetic because judge reads the doc comment attached to the statement head, so every name in one statement is judged against the SAME comment and produces the same verdict, which means judging once per statement is behaviourally equivalent for pass or fail. The second case is a genuine hole: no judgement happens, so no verdict exists.

An exported destructuring pattern with no doc comment is reported as a violation naming the pattern; an exported statement with several declarators is judged; neither change introduces a false positive on a documented export
